answers.answer: Put the helper in braces inside the reply box, among your own words. On the main path: open Commands in the sidebar, choose your command, add {user} in Reply, choose Save changes at the right of the footer, then type the command's trigger in Twitch chat. Everything outside the braces goes out as typed, and each helper is swapped for its value when the reply runs.
answers.quote: In Reply, add {user} where your name should go.

answers.answer: You need a command that sends a reply, from the Before you start section. If you have none, Create a command shows how to make one. For viewer text, Viewer Templates must be on (it is in Features, in the Chat group, and on by default) and the viewer must hold the template permission (Subscribers and higher by default).
answers.quote: You need a command that sends a reply.

answers.answer: Success means the bot's reply in chat shows your name where you typed {user}. Each place has different helpers: commands have the person and the command words, event responses have the event values but no command words, timers have only the shared helpers. A typo shows the warning "Not a known helper here:" under the box, "is not a recognized template helper" on save means no helper has that name, and "is not available in" means the helper exists but not in this place.
answers.quote: The bot’s reply shows your name where you typed {user}.

answers.answer: A helper copied from an event response often needs that event, and a chat command does not carry it. For example, {gifter} pasted into a command reply makes the save refuse it, and the message names the places where it works: event responses and pipelines. The author should check the helper against the command's own suggestions (type { or use Show all helpers) and pick one that works in commands.
answers.quote: If you paste {gifter} from an event response into a command reply, the message ends with “It works in: event responses, pipelines”.

answers.answer: The Both row of the Send the reply to table speaks of a reply with HTML on before the page says where the HTML switch is, so I scrolled on to find it. It costs one forward detour but does not block a step.
answers.quote: The HTML switch is right below Send the reply to.
